newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk 4-mth budget gap 520 trln lira - opposition.
newsitem.headline: Turk 4-mth budget gap 520 trln lira - opposition.

text.p: Turkey's main opposition leader said on Wednesday he had obtained information that the budget gave a deficit of 520 trillion lira in the first four months of 1997 despite the government's target of a balanced budget.

"According to information that has reached me, there was a 520 trillion lira deficit in April and the budget deficit (for 1997) will be around 2,000 trillion lira," Motherland Party leader Mesut Yilmaz told his MPs.
The government has not released any budget figures this year, but various sources have estimated the four-month deficit at over 300 trillion lira.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan admitted in late April that "big difficulties" began to emerge in March after a balanced budget in the first two months of the year.
The budget deficit for 1996 was 1,218 trillion lira.
Yilmaz said Turkey's foreign debts currently equalled $80 billion and domestic debts stood at 3,600 trillion lira.
"Interest payments (on domestic debt) in the January-April period in 1995 were 195 trillion, for the same period in 1996, they were 434 trillion and in January-April 1997, 633 trillion," Yilmaz said.
